utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate that, Your Honour. And I apologise, Your Honour. I tried to do it through the proper channels, and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I did not want to be late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness JJ. How are you? Did you have a nice lunch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, not as good as Spanish lunches are, but it was good enough. Thank you. I'm fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess what I meant to ask you right before lunch was not who was the main commander of the HVO on the day you arrived, but you were there from mid-April to, what, the end of September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, then, who was the main commander for the HVO during that time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I need to remember that, because questions that you're asking me, you're asking me all about things that happened nine years ago. You're asking me about a period which covered six months of my life, from the moment that I arrive in Bosnia -- Bosnia. I think that the chief persons, the commander of the HVO, was Brigadier Lasic. Then there was Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: By the way -- and I appreciate your answer that it was many years ago, and you were a young man then, I take it. How old were you then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Twenty-four.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Was this your first assignment abroad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I have asked Madam Registrar to give me a temporary number on a document I have handed her in English. It's nine copies, and I would ask the usher to show Witness JJ that document to refresh his recollection. While the usher's doing that, I will ask a few questions, if it's appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: JJ, you indicated that your headquarters were in Medjugorje; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: At the headquarters, you kept the -- a list, your battalion did, a list of Croat civilians, HVO, and also Muslim civilians, Muslim military, and Croat military figures; did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You have in front of you a document which I do not know the number of yet, but I'm asking you to please thumb through that and look at it while I get a number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could interpreters have a copy, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number will be D1/32.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: While the usher is giving the interpreter the documents, I would explain to you, Witness JJ, that this document now marked D1/32 was provided to Defence counsel by the Office of the Prosecutor through a statement by a -- by an officer in your brigade, which I won't mention in open session right now. I believe the interpreters have the document. So have you looked at the document D1/32?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: -- seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Not in English, but in Spanish, I think that it could have been drawn up by us. But I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you were still in the country of Bosnia-Herzegovina on 11 September 1993. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And your battalion kept a list such as D1/32 of Croat civilians, Croat military, Muslim civilians, Muslim military. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Could be. Could be. Could be. Could be that we had something similar, or perhaps it could be this document. But translated from Spanish, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And Witness JJ, I know that you've indicated you were used sometimes as a translator for non-English speaking people in the area -- in Mostar. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So you can read this document in English, can you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So just a moment ago, you, I think, indicated that your knowledge or recollection is Mr. Praljak was the head of the HVO. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No. I mentioned Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And do you see him on this document? Be the third page of the document, but on the lower right-hand corner, where you see page 6-6.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That shows Petkovic as being the general of the HVO. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It also shows, underneath him, Slobodan Praljak as brigadier general. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Underneath that is Zarko Tole, brigadier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: If you just look down yourself, do these names all ring a bell with you, and then to the right, as to who they might have been? For example --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I repeat that Balkan names, quite unintelligible for Spaniards. And you keep asking me about the year 1993. If you ask me now about a player in the Royal Madrid soccer team, that I could remember and tell you. But -- if you had photographs here. But like this, you put before me some names like this. The chief ones, yes; Petkovic does ring a bell. Ivan Andabak, Bosic; but hundred percent, I simply don't remember them. And at that time, I suppose I would have known all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And for example, to move on to page -- lower on page what shows 69, you have on the top, under Muslim Military, you have Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you remember that name from your time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I spent three days with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: By the way, Witness JJ, these names are very hard for me also, so don't feel alone. The purpose, though, of your battalion making a list like this, can you tell the Trial Chamber what was the purpose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes. This is just a directory. It is very important to have when one has to establish contact with somebody from the authorities or somebody in authority, then, of one of the factions. As you can see, Slobodan Bosic, then you have his secretary's number, the secretariat, his mobile, and all the other information necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the people named on this list would have been the higher-ranking military and civilian people in the area; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No. It could be people at a lower ranking, people who nevertheless could be of some use to us for some type of contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: But nevertheless, some person who had some authority in the area of Mostar that you would need to make contact with would probably be on this list, whether they were high or low?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: The important -- to be important in the area was the -- was the necessary condition but not the only, not the indispensable condition to find one's name on this list. What I'm trying to say, there could be people with tremendous power in the area yet who perhaps do not figure on these lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You've looked at the list. Mr. Mladen Naletilic, his name is nowhere to be found on this list, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: While you're looking, do you know what city Mr. Mladen Naletilic was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No, as a matter of fact, I don't. I didn't, and I don't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: There's been much evidence in this Trial Chamber, since this trial started on September 10th, that Mr. Mladen Naletilic was from the town of Siroki Brijeg. Does that ring any bells with you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: You are taking me into an area which I don't understand. I do not recall 99 per cent of the things from that time. I merely refer to the documents that I have before me, and this, yes, indeed this I can explain. I can explain how this is done, what are the sources, but those kind of questions, I can't answer them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Was your recollection of the events that you lived through back in 1993 fresher in your memory on November 6th of 2000 when you gave your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor at The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: My statement is a general statement which does not go into detail, and especially concerning persons or places.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you not recall talking, in your statement that you gave, about a man named Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No. I merely said that I accompanied my superior, my -- to some meetings with him, and I gave a sort of a general description.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And in your general description that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor in November of 2000, do you recall telling them that you could not put Tuta in an HVO military hierarchy, nor did he belong to HVO at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you further recall, Witness JJ, that you told the OTP at that time that you think he was more civilian than a soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I am referring to my -- I'm referring you to my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And I'm trying to refresh your recollection is all. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Very kind of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall telling the Office of the Prosecutor, in November of 2000 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Some time ago there was a ruling by the Trial Chamber that all witness statements should be shown to the witness if the party who is interviewing a witness -- examining a witness refers to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you for reminding me. I will do it right now. I apologise. There's nine copies; one for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness JJ, while these are being distributed, you might go straight to page 6 of the English translation. And while you're looking at that, I might direct your attention to the bottom 25 per cent of the page. Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Is it true that you said that you thought that Tuta was more civilian than soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And that you also stated that he was a very charismatic and prestigious person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You also told the OTP that Tuta and Ivan Andabak were well-known people, and everybody talked about them and how they thought; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you know from your personal experience and being an intelligence officer in Bosnia in 1993 that Ivan Andabak and Tuta, or Mr. Naletilic, had fought against the Serbs in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And they had fought alongside the Muslims in that battle against Serb aggression?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Is this, to your belief and knowledge, where the knowledge that everybody talked about how they fought, is this where it came from, the battles with the Serbs, or do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would ask you, Witness JJ, if you could please look at Exhibit P405. Page 4 in the English, and I don't... Under Mostar, you discuss -- it was discussed in direct testimony about a meeting held in Medjugorje, I believe. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And if I recall your direct testimony, you stated that there was -- there was present at that meeting "the presence of major political and military figures of authority in the area." Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber, who were these people who had major political and military authority in the area that were at this meeting in Medjugorje on the 9th of May, 1993? 19th of May, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: There should be a reference in the document. But it doesn't really important that the presidents of Croatia and Bosnia [as interpreted]. That is the presence that counts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, it is. And I'm asking you, can you recall the names of these high-ranking important figures in the military and political circles in the area that were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I believe there was Franjo Tudjman, and there would have been Izetbegovic. Then General Petkovic, I believe I saw him there, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: This was not an occasion that you saw Mr. Mladen Naletilic, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I cannot really say, but I don't think he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In reading your testimony from this morning, you participated in more than just this meeting on the 19th of May, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No, I did not participate in the meetings. I was there to -- as a support, that is, bringing together, meeting those leaders, telling them where to go, directing them to the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I apologise, Witness JJ. I didn't mean it in that fashion. You were present at the meetings, doing what you just testified to, not participating.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: That's right. Yes, I was present. I was present at the headquarters, at the entrance into the conference hall if they needed something.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber approximately how many other of these meetings, this type of meetings, were you present when the leaders from the HVO and the ABiH and people from your battalion tried to get things settled down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: That was a very special meeting because, naturally, meetings were between local leaders. The problem that one had at the HVO level, that is, the main staff, was in our area. But Halilovic was never in our area. And this meeting was a very special one. It was a very high-level meeting. Apart from that, there were other meetings when we usually focused on our area of responsibility, on Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: For example -- now that you mentioned Mostar, you mentioned a meeting that you were present at which concerned General Pellnas. Do you remember that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And was also Mr. Petkovic there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I think I recognised him on a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In all of the meetings that you attended by your presence, my client, Tuta, was never involved in any of those meetings, was he, Witness JJ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No, that is true. He was not at any one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And just for the record, the statement that you gave on the 6th day of November, 2000 to this Tribunal, which you have in front of you, you've read that statement and signed it, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And the document I show you is a true and correct copy of your original statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In your direct testimony, you testified that you spoke sometimes or on several occasions with Tuta. Was that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: The testimony says that I was -- that he was present as a leader -- that I was present with my superior at some meetings. But those clearly were not official meetings. They were not formal meetings. Those were meetings when you sit down and you can talk, but I wasn't the one who was leading those conversations, that was conducting those conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I completely understood, Witness JJ. I want to take you back to this individual named Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: He was married to a Spanish woman; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall going to his home for a birthday party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Have you ever been to Mr. Ivan Andabak's home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And did you -- about how many times was it that you even met Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: A couple of times. He wasn't my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you speak Croatian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: None of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you speak German?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: A little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: How did you converse with Mr. Naletilic? Which language did you use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: There were interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And can you tell me - and I know it's hard because it's been many years - approximately how long did these couple of meetings even last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: You're asking me things that to me -- Mr. Tuta wasn't my responsibility, and therefore, for me, it was of no relevance. It is an aspect which is not relevant, and therefore, I do not remember about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you for your honest answer. What you're saying is that during the period of time that you were in the Mostar area, that Tuta was basically an irrelevant person and you didn't take any notice of him. Isn't that what you just said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I've told you already that we had some compartmentation of our work. He was not my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And is it true that you never had access to this Ivan Andabak's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You indicated also that people in Mostar and in the Southern Bosnia-Herzegovina area, in the time period that you were there, they wore all kinds of uniforms. Is this a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Would this be a fact for both the ABiH army and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Would it be hard to determine a soldier being in the ABiH army or HVO army because they wore the same type, colour uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, it was difficult to tell them apart. Even they found it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. difficult. It was really chaos as regards military uniforms. There were no standardised military uniforms at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You also testified that in Mostar during the time period that you were there, that there was extreme tension between these two communities because they were both killing each other all the time. True?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And that there was hatred on both sides. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: When you were speaking about Doljani, Sovici, Jablanica, you indicated that you can't remember whether you ever went to these locations.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I think you were not really listening to what I stated this morning. I told you that the information on these villages we got from our people in Slavonika [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: My question to you is: Did you physically go to Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, but not at the time when this operation mentioned earlier took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: When did you go to Sovici? What month, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: It's impossible for me to tell you this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: How about Jablanica? Did you travel to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Approximately how many times, JJ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Ten times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you observe any of what you termed earlier in your testimony ethnic cleansing of Croats in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You were often in East Mostar, I take it; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you go to the elementary school in East Mostar where the Croat prisoners were being held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Were you not allowed to go there or chose not to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Are you doubting on the fact that I'm a neutral person?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No. I'm just asking you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I don't advise you to go along those lines any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, my question to you is: Did you go to the elementary school in East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: How can I put it? I don't even remember a building that could be the elementary school in --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Witness, please settle down. If you don't remember, please tell me you don't remember and I'll go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No. But I don't like this sort of question with another question behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Nobody likes to be on the witness stand. Okay. You have a multitude of SpaBat documents in front of you; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In your estimates, Witness JJ, are these the entire documents generated by SpaBat during the time period that you were in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can you give me an estimate, if you can, as to how many other documents that there might be available that were generated by SpaBat during the time period you were in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I can only make a sort of an evaluation, sort of rough evaluation of my G-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, a INTREP per day, one INSUM every 15 days, and documents that were drafted ad hoc, on an ad hoc basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could you look at Document 537, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I haven't got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You've got it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I haven't got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You don't have 537? It's in this blue binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, what is the number of that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, P537.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is it 357?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It's 537, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In this binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In an earlier binder delivered to us and the Trial Chamber from Mr. Prelec of the OTP. He testified about certain UNPROFOR documents and additional SpaBat documents.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Is that a document generated through your --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No, it wasn't drafted by us, because it says SITREP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, could you look at it anyway.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, but I won't make any comments on a document that was not under our responsibility. If you understood what I said this morning, the SITREP documents were done by another section, different from ours. I had nothing to do with them, and I don't know what they could have included in their documents they drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, Witness JJ: Did you have something to do with every document that's in the file in front of you? Yes, that one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: But nothing to do with 537 at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: But your answer to the other question is you did have something to do with the documents in front of you in that binder, in the binder that you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I would have to look at the documents one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: If you can turn to page 5 out of 8 of Document 537, I would just like you to read to yourself subparagraph (k).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object because the witness stated that he had nothing to do with the document, which is SITREP. G-3 was in charge of SITREP documents, and it was clarified during the direct examination in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you that the witness has already said that he will not answer any questions related to the documents which he is not familiar with, did not prepare. Mr. Meek, would you please skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, my question would not be about the document itself. I just wanted him to read the paragraph, and then I have a question for him because he was in Mostar as an intelligence agent for six, eight months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have to know the point of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The point, Your Honour, is this: The point is this document was generated in July of 1993 during a time period this witness was acting as the intelligence officer for his battalion. And he was all around the area. And I want to ask him a question about -- not exactly the document or how it was prepared, but something that's contained in the document to see if he can verify it. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: He doesn't need to look at the document to do that. Ask him the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Judge. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness JJ, while you were in Bosnia-Herzegovina during the months that you were there in 1993, did it come in to your knowledge through all of the sources that you had in your battalion of terrorist actions by the Islamic militants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, there were some news about Islamic militants, radical militants, that could be operating in the area. But it wasn't our main concern at all because, in our area of operations, we didn't have any evidence that these people were working in the area. They were mostly working in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And when you say "Central Bosnia," tell the Trial Chamber how many kilometres it would be from Central Bosnia to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't matter whether it's close or not; it's whether the area is under our responsibility or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So can we agree that it's very close from Central Bosnia to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: You come to a conclusion I didn't give you. Central Bosnia belonged -- was under the responsibility of a different brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I totally understand you, JJ. My only question is, geographically, it's not very far --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you become aware during your tenure in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993 of the booklet put out entitled "Instructions for an Islamic" -- "for a Muslim Soldier"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems to me that this document has been already discussed in the Trial Chamber, and also the problem with relevancy to the case was also discussed. No need to raise this question again. It's quite -- completely irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, it has been asked and answered. I'm going forward. I'm done. I just wanted to know if he heard about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In Document 357, Witness JJ, which I think that you can testify about, can you look at it, please. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: [In English] 357?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, sir, 357. In direct examination, you indicated, I think, and please correct me if I'm wrong - I think you will anyway - did you go to Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I've already told you that I probably went there, but I don't really remember exactly when I did go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. But my notes indicated that you testified - maybe you didn't - that this city or town or village had been half destroyed. My question to you is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Where did I say this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Perhaps the document said that, not you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I think that you got a problem with doctrine, dear sir. This is not -- this does not reflect words of mine. This reflects information received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can you tell me --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I did not make this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did it come from one of your units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And does it have a credibility rating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: If it came from one of our units, it has credibility rating. Some of the information from Doljani could come from other sources of information and would not be as credible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And can you tell me, by looking at document 357, what was the credibility rating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: If you look at the beginning of the document, you will realise it's C2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So it's in the middle grade even though it comes from your unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I've explained before --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: -- that -- I don't think it's worthwhile repeating. The credibility or reliability is the less credibility of a group of documents by INTREP. That's why it's got C2 rating. But if you look at this document -- well, if it's C2, if at the same time it is mentioned that one of our units has read it, this piece of information has A credibility rating.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I've just read your last answer from the transcript monitor, and it appears, Witness JJ, that the document itself has a C2 rating, but you said it has an A rating. Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it wasn't adequately translated what I said. I'm going to explain the process of evaluation once again. Perhaps it would have been better for you to listen more carefully to what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, I understand the rating, how you do it. My only question to you is: Which rating did this document get? That's all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: As I told you, that it's got a C2 rating. Why? Because it receives the lowest level of all evaluations of the different types of information that are part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: So that I gave you an example of this. If within this C2 report there is one piece of information that comes from one of our units, this information will not be a C2 information. It will be an A information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. And it may be in the translation. So I'm not meaning to upset you, Witness. I truly am not. Tell me, if you know, who negotiated in Jablanica. If you know. If you don't, just tell me you don't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Who negotiated what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Negotiated a calming of the tensions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, basically, the catalysing agent in Jablanica were the commanders of a Spanish unit in the area, perhaps with the support of the HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And if you know, and you may not, who were the HVO officials who would have been negotiating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I have no idea at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. During your tenure in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993, did you become aware of any information from any source about Mujahedin in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: What area, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The area of Central Bosnia, Mostar, Siroki Brijeg, Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, if we're referring to Bosnia, we did get information about the possible presence of Mujahedins.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And were these Mujahedin coming from the Middle East or Middle East countries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes. We would say from Arab countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And did you, from the sources of information that you gathered, learn also that there was funding for these Mujahedin coming from the Arab countries?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems to me that this question was not within the scope of witness commission in Bosnia, and now it is not relevant to the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek. We don't believe that this question is relevant to the issue. Would you please skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness JJ, I have read the report. Would it be fair to say that, for whatever reasons, that you may have had more contact with Muslims than Croats or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness JJ, a few more questions and then I'll be finished, hopefully. Do you recall the name of the interpreter you mentioned when you were with your commanding officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I don't remember the names of any interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you observe what kind of discipline there was in the HVO army in the months that you were in Bosnia-Herzegovina in the Mostar area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, if we compare this with a regular army, such as that of NATO, their chain of command was not really very well defined. This is my own personal opinion. And the commanders in chief did not really control the operations. This is a personal opinion of mine, a feeling I got by observing the situation. But I haven't seen any proof of lack of discipline at certain levels. For instance, I went with one of the chiefs of HVO in his vehicle, and one of the checkpoints wouldn't let us through. But taking into account details such as this, I came to the conclusion that the channel of command wasn't very clear, and the way that operations were conducted either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And I think in your statement, you had mentioned the fact that when you and your commander -- or at least, your commander and you were present -- attempted to have a meeting in Mostar to have joint HVO and BiH details, but it didn't work. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No, no, no. You haven't understood anything that I said. I think you mean the joint commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's what I meant, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: The joint commission was a forum which was organised principally for the people who came from the United Nations, and I don't mean UNPROFOR only because there were also representatives of the European Union. And even more civilians were there than the military. So it wasn't a debating forum, a forum to discuss strictly military issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Perhaps we've misunderstood each other. On page 3 of your statement to the OTP, you talk about the negotiations with --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: These were not the negotiations of the joint commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No, no, no, I understand that. Just listen to my question, please. You've already testified today about General Pellnas's meeting in Mostar. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Vaguely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And Pellnas had an idea to establish joint patrols between Bosniaks and Croats. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That didn't work, did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Indeed, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It didn't work because, as you've indicated at least in your written statement, that everybody in Mostar who had a gun considered himself to be a policeman. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: It is. But to try to explain to the person who interviewed me, because that is what civil wars look like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And in your opinion, this was a civil war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, if we consider that this was happening in one and the same country. I do not know whether that is the legal term, whether legally this is a civil war, but in my view as a military man, if you have two sides in one and the same country fighting one another, then this is, to my mind, a civil war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness JJ, you've indicated in your statement that you and General Pellnas even slept in the HVO headquarters in Mostar. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we spent a night -- that is, I spent part of that night patrolling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That was my question. Was it only one night or two nights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: For me, I think it was one night only, or perhaps there were two. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I would like you to look at Document 401 briefly. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: For the record, this is a document dated 18 May, 1993. And on page 5 of the English, there's a comment. You may want to turn to English or Spanish; either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Was the Bosnian Serb army shelling Mostar so that they could exploit the situation and the prevailing confusion to ensure the continuation of the conflict between the Muslims and the Croats? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: As I explained this morning, all of this which is under "Comment" is the analyst's view that need not be true at all. It may be just a conclusion of the person who analyzed that piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, on the other hand, Witness JJ, it may be a hundred percent true. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: This is just a comment. It is not information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The comments -- tell me, aren't comments made from the information that you receive, as an information officer, from various locations and various sources?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No. The problem is that the interpretation was not correct. A comment in this case, it's -- it means a hypothetical, a new line of investigation - that is what the comment is - which may lead to nowhere or may produce something. One constantly works, analyses, because there may be dozens of hypotheses. And for this, this is put as a comment, so the one who reads it can know what he is reading, that this is a personal opinion, that this is a hypothesis, not something that is hundred percent true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Fair enough. Do you know -- if you know, to your personal knowledge, did your unit or any other units from your government that were in Bosnia-Herzegovina follow up on that comment that the Bosnian Serb army was shelling East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No. It would be very difficult to confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Please look at 424. Document 424, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You don't?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No, I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness JJ, if you could look at page 4 of the English translation, right in the middle of the page. Did you become aware about -- on or about the 30th of May, 1993, that the rumours had continued to circulate about mass detention, possible mass detention of Muslim men by the HVO? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And did you also know that at least on May 30, 1993, there was no evidence that this was happening? Isn't that what your report says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: But just a moment. I need to read the Spanish version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, that is quite right. It was translated correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: My last question to you, sir, or questions, hopefully only one, would be: Since you testified you did travel to Jablanica approximately ten times, you had to go through checkpoints manned by the ABiH army, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes. And the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No, no, no. On the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes. On the way, you went through both checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall, Witness JJ, if you do recall, were there more ABiH checkpoints in that area or more HVO checkpoints? And if you don't know, I understand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I don't understand. There were a number of checkpoints of different sides. I don't really remember how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: One last question, if you can answer it. Did the ABiH army specifically allow SpaBat units to go to the front lines with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No. Now I don't really remember. I don't know if it is any document, whether our people there were informed about something like that. Whether they went with them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness JJ, you're in the intelligence service for your army; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, I haven't explained the organisation of the army and all the services. I was merely the intelligence officer of the Canarias group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In layman's terms for a non-military officer, would that also be what would also be called a spy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness JJ, I want to thank you very much. It's been a pleasure to listen to your testimony. Thank you for coming to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Meek. Mr. Seric, cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness JJ, my name is Branko Seric, and I represent Vinko Martinovic. Could you tell us, please, very briefly, as briefly as possible, what was the function of the Spanish Battalion at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Basically, the function was the support to the United Nations personnel in matters of the distribution of humanitarian aid, monitoring of the security situation, and encouragement to all the options that could bring about the abating of the tension and including the cessation of hostilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us now, within the scope of those tasks of your battalion, what was the function of your own intelligence work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: I've already explained it. It was to obtain, to procure information so as to evaluate it and so that the superiors could then take decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When collecting information, did you avail yourselves, among other sources, the Muslim secret intelligence service, AID? Was that one of your sources?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No. No. Let's see. We are now entering an area which -- we have certain sources, but at that level, to talk about secret services, we were not -- we were not members -- that is, we were part of the tactical information so that the commands could evaluate this and take decisions. We were not talking about any secret services.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Who collected information for you on the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Well, I've already explained it. Units deployed on the ground, that was the principal source. And contacts and interviews that we had always open with the different representatives of different factions. And also, we received information from superior echelons of the UNPROFOR and collateral units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: That is what I was asking. In the process of the collection of information from various sources, that is, as a result of work on the ground, can you exclude the possibility that the information that reached the people collecting information may have been also obtained from the Muslim secret service, AID?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, that could be, but nobody was ever introduced himself or nobody was identified ever as a member of any such service on either of the two sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I quite understand that because no intelligence officer will reveal his job openly, because then he wouldn't be able to do his work. So that is why I'm asking you to what extent you evaluated the quality of the sources of information and not just the quality of the information itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: It depends on things. Of course, we have to evaluate both these things. One evaluates the source when one analyses the whole background and all the information, and one also analyses within the context, and one analyses the information within the context within which it was received.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that I understand correctly that you personally did not collect information on the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes, it was only when I had contacts. It was always open talking, doing interviews, not using any secret, any covert means of work or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you personally -- were you personally involved in selecting information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: The information was collected by all the members of the G-2. No, this is not what I said. I said that the evaluation of the information was a decision which was joint of all the members of the G-2, that is, having studied all the aspects that I already mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: My question was whether information was selected and the documents connected to that information, or do we find in these binders everything that you collected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yeah, I see. Now I understand what you're asking. Well, yes, there is a certain selection. But what is eliminated -- what was eliminated at the time were residual things, completely, completely irrelevant or, shall I say, silly things, for instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric, we believe that this question has been asked by Mr. Meek already. You have to avoid the repetition of asking the same questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, for your instructions. I only have two or three more questions, and then I'm through with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Who analysed the information? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Members of the G-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Have you ever serviced any other Court with your information in any other legal institution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I am going to make a submission, and it's up to you to respond with yes or no. In my submission, after having heard your testimony today, and I have the binders which my client has not been able to review because they haven't been translated into his mother tongue, so we were not able to analyse them together, this is a pile of indications and reports carried -- collected on the ground in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: This is information received from all the sources, as I already explained. That is, our units, interviews conducted by our people, people who were monitors, who then told us about the interviews they had, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I do not have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to direct the witness to Exhibit 407, page 5, English version; page 3, Spanish version. This document is dated 20th of May, '93, INTREP. One question: Just paragraph 3 at the top in the English version. Does this document contain information that, by that time, by the 20th of May, some prisoners from Heliodrom had been released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: The question is?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, that the prisoners had been released and were being released.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: The reference here, it says that after a meeting of the joint commission, there should be a visit to the Heliodrom, and it says that the HVO members should -- that they would immediately release the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: One paragraph down, please. That's about buses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke about that this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The same document. It was already examined by you. My next question will be: I would like you to open the document Exhibit 474, dated the 2nd of June, 1993. Page 4, English version; page 3, Spanish version. Under the heading "Jablanica," just paragraph 2. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Does this document contain information that in the area there are HVO troops of Jusuf Prazina, "Juka," as written, and Mladen Naletilic, written "aka Tuta"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes. But this information, it is below another heading which says "Other Information," and these are miscellaneous items here, and the -- it would be -- it would have one of the lowest credibility ratings at this stage here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And my last question will be -- let's turn to Exhibit 476. This is INTREP 212, 23rd of June, 1993. Page 4, 5, English version; page 3, 4, Spanish version. The same, under the heading "Jablanica," paragraph 1, 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's the same thing. It comes under the heading "Other Information." Had there been other information that could properly be corroborated and verified, then it would have received a much -- a much more prominent place. This could be just a commentary. And it is left in the text, but -- I mean, just as in the previous case, that is, other business, other matter, again a miscellaneous.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... there is some comment that commanders of special units, groups, like Juka and Tuta, have left the area and are present in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: This is a comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JJ
utterances.text: There is no evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It is time to break. We will resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 7th day of November, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
